raw_response:
I have only 8 mu, so I will keep it simple and do cotton the way I know works here. I will use the kind of seed I saw do well on nearby fields, not the old weak seed. Last year and in other years, if cotton is short and yellow early, the yield drops and I cannot make that back later, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the field go hungry. I will put enough base fertilizer before planting, then add more nitrogen later when the plants start growing hard and setting squares. Our place has well water, so if the rain is short I will not wait too long, because cotton in dry soil stays small. I will spray several times because if aphids, red spiders, or bollworms get ahead of me, they eat the money right off the field. For land preparation, I will have it ploughed first so the soil is loose and the roots can go down. If the season is normal, I will aim for a little over 300 jin of seed cotton per mu, around 160 kilos or so. On 8 mu, that is worth the input if the weather does not turn bad.
